answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks through hardware remote attestation. Nodes run inside secure enclaves acting as a cryptographic quill, signing proofs with fused silicon keys. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of buying physical processors per alias rather than virtualizing instances. Relays check these proofs during surges that streak by like a comet, pruning nodes whose activity cools to an ember. However, this relies on centralized chipmakers and risks side-channel attacks.
